events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $5.00 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The trace settles the governing path: the rider pressed cancel (cancelled_by = rider) [F2], the driver was never at the pickup by scheduled time + 5 min, in fact never came within 200 m of the pickup and no arrival was ever recorded [F1][F5][F6][F4], and the driver made 0 in-app messages and 0 calls before the cancellation [F3]. On those facts the rider's cancellation falls squarely in NS-8: she cancelled 8 minutes after the 09:52 scheduled pickup, i.e. past scheduled time + 5 minutes, with the driver not there, so the fee charged on record is refundable in full — "a fee charged → refund_full" [F4][F7][NS-8]. The driver's own line of defence does not reach that text: NS-4 charges a rider cancellation fee only in the ordinary case, and it cannot stand where the record shows the driver was 4069 m away and had made no contact attempt throughout the free wait [F1][F3][NS-4]. The trace's own NS-8 checks pass on both limbs [F4][F1][F2][F3].

what_would_change: Had the driver reached the pickup by the scheduled time + 5 minutes, the rider's cancellation would fall under NS-4 instead, and had he messaged or called, no goodwill credit would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to it was 4069 m at 10:00:00 and he never came within 200 m, so no arrival condition can be met.
The platform recorded no arrival at all — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was logged (driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are both null).
Before cancelling, the driver sent zero in-app messages and made zero in-app calls, so the mandatory contact requirement for a no-show fee is unmet.

The rider waited the full free-wait period: scheduled pickup was 09:52:00 and the rider cancelled at 10:00:00, 8 minutes later, i.e. she gave the driver more than the 5-minute free wait and even the 8-minute record threshold before cancelling.
The rider's app reason for cancelling was "driver_taking_too_long", not a rider no-show, and a $5.00 fee was nonetheless charged, so the charge must be voided and refunded in full.

The driver's post-trip statement that "traffic was very heavy on the way to the pickup" does not excuse the failure: no traffic incident was recorded near the route, weather was fair, and a verbal excuse given after the fact is not the required in-app message or call before the wait expired.

The driver's history shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld (both no-show) in the last 90 days, supporting an account-review add-on; the rider's profile shows 0 disputes in 90 days and no no-shows, which supports her credibility.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled on her own initiative (F2), so the case turns on the fee being unauthorised rather than on a driver cancellation; the driver will argue NS-4 (rider cancellation after 3 minutes) to say a $5.00 fee is in principle chargeable.

The driver will point to congestion on LOYANG AVENUE, band 2 (10–19 km/h) between 09:42 and 10:05 (F13), and his statement about heavy traffic (F12), to argue he was delayed by conditions and the wait should be excused.
The rider's own messages (F9, F10) show she was present and able to cancel, which the driver may use to argue the ride was still available to her had she waited longer.

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled this trip: the timeline records the cancellation at 10:00:00, 13 minutes after acceptance, so the case is governed by NS-4 (rider cancellation), not by any driver no-show cancellation.
The $5.00 on record is the standard rider-cancellation fee under NS-4, charged because the rider cancelled after 3 minutes of matching (13 minutes after acceptance).

The only alternative route to a full refund is NS-8 (driver did not arrive by scheduled time + 5 min), but that clause governs a rider cancellation made because the driver failed to appear — and the rider here was still charged under a rider-cancellation reason ('driver_taking_too_long') rather than a driver-failure cancellation, so the fee cannot be treated as void on the NS-1 conditions, which only arise where the driver cancels for no-show.

The driver remained reachable and in service throughout: his account is 6.1 years old with 911 trips in 90 days and a 4.47 rating, which is inconsistent with a deliberate non-arrival and supports denying a $5.00 goodwill credit.
The rider's own account is clean (0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days), so no flag_account against either party is warranted from the profiles; profile facts do not decide this case.

weaknesses: The GPS record is fatal to an arrival defence: F1 shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 4069 m at 10:00:00 and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1(i) (arrival with GPS inside 200 m) fails outright.
The platform never recorded arrival at all — F5 (driver_arrived_at is null) and F6 (never tapped "I'm Here", no auto-arrival) — which the rider will use to argue NS-8 applies.

The rider wrote two unanswered messages, 09:52 (F9) and 09:59 (F10), and F3 shows the driver sent 0 messages and made 0 calls before 10:00:00, so the rider's complaint that 'he never messaged or called me' is supported by the timeline, not contradicted.

The rider cancelled 8 minutes after the 09:52 scheduled pickup (F4), which is past the scheduled + 5 min line in NS-8, so the rider's NS-8 argument is live; the only counter is that the cancellation was recorded under a rider-cancellation reason with no driver no-show cancellation (F2).

The driver's statement 'Traffic was very heavy on the way to the pickup' (F12) is a statement only; the traffic record shows congestion only on LOYANG AVENUE, band 2, 09:42–10:05 (F13), with no incidents near the route (F14) — and RD-4 traffic reasoning is not accepted in the no-show clause anyway; a 4069 m gap is not explained by band-2 congestion.
The driver's profile carries 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17), which the rider can use to argue a pattern, even though RD-6 repeat logic does not apply to this rider-cancellation case.

points.response: Conceded that the rider pressed cancel (F2). That fact does not move the case: NS-0 sends a case to NS-4 only where the rider cancels for her own reasons within the free window; the rider waited 8 minutes past the scheduled pickup (F4) with the driver 4069 m away and never within 200 m (F1) and no arrival recorded (F5, F6), so NS-8 governs and any fee charged is refundable in full.

There is no lawful basis to charge the $5.00: NS-4 permits it only when the rider cancels in the ordinary course, but the text of NS-8 gives the rider a free cancellation where the driver is not at the pickup by scheduled time + 5 min (F4: cancelled 8 minutes after 09:52:00, F5/F6: no arrival ever recorded, F1: 4069 m away), and the fee must therefore be refunded in full.

This reads NS-8 backwards. NS-8 grants the rider the right to cancel free when the driver has not arrived by scheduled time + 5 minutes; it does not require the driver to have cancelled, and the driver's failure here is documented on the system record, not on the rider's app reason (F4, F5, F6, F1, F3). The driver's 0 messages and 0 calls (F3) also fail NS-1(iii), so no NS-1 fee can stand either.

The driver's tenure and trip count (F17) do not cure the record: the GPS places him 4069 m from the pickup at 10:00:00 and never inside 200 m (F1), and a 4069 m gap is not explained by congestion confined to LOYANG AVENUE at 10–19 km/h (F13) with no incident near the route (F14) and fair weather (F15).

Agreed that the rider's clean profile (F16) is not itself a ground for a flag. The account-review request rests on the driver's record — 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show, in 90 days (F17) — which NS-9/RD-6 pattern logic supports as an add-on only, the finding itself coming from F1, F4, F5 and F6.

Conceded as a fact — F1 and F5 show the driver never reached the pickup and the platform never logged an arrival — but NS-1/NS-2 are the wrong clauses: they govern a fee charged when the DRIVER cancels for rider no-show, and here the rider cancelled (F2), so NS-1's arrival condition is not an element of this charge at all.

Conceded that no arrival was recorded (F5, F6), but that matters only under NS-1, which applies to a driver-initiated no-show cancellation; the cancellation here was the rider's own act at 10:00:00 (F2), so the null arrival fields do not void the rider-cancellation fee under NS-4.

Agreed that the driver sent no message and made no call before 10:00:00 (F3; only the rider wrote, F9, F10) — the contact condition is an NS-1 element, and NS-1 is reached only when the driver cancels for no-show (NS-0), which he did not.

Conceded that the rider cancelled 8 minutes after the 09:52 scheduled pickup (F4, F2); note this cuts both ways — NS-8's line is scheduled time + 5 min and the free wait under NS-1 is 5 minutes, so the fact she waited 8 minutes is not itself evidence the fee was unauthorised.

The recorded reason is the rider's own app selection ('driver_taking_too_long', F2), not a driver cancellation, so NS-2 (voiding a no-show fee) and NS-3 (driver cancelled for another reason) do not apply; NS-4 fixes the $5.00 fee precisely for a rider who cancels more than 3 minutes after matching (F2, F7).

Not contested: the driver's after-the-fact statement (F12) is a statement only, no incident was recorded near the route (F14), weather was fair (F15), and the only congestion was band 2 on LOYANG AVENUE (F13) — none of which supplies the in-app chat or call NS-1 requires, and none of which is needed for the rider's own NS-4 cancellation fee to stand.

The driver's profile (F17: 3 disputes, 2 upheld, 6.1-year account, 911 trips/90 d) may support an account-review add-on but cannot create an outcome here, and NS-9's flag is for repeat RIDER no-shows; the rider's clean profile (F16) likewise does not void an NS-4 rider-cancellation fee.

I stand by the fee: NS-4 charges $5.00 where a rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching, and F2 shows a 13-minute gap; the rider's own evidence (F9, F10) shows she had contact with the platform before cancelling, so the record supports a chargeable rider cancellation rather than a voided fee.
